Answer: C
Reason: The CT images (Figures 4a and 4b) clearly show hyperdense, radiopaque material within the pulmonary arteries, which is characteristic of polymethylmethacrylate (bone cement). This finding, combined with the history of recent vertebroplasty and a sudden drop in end-tidal CO2 (indicating increased dead space ventilation from vascular obstruction), confirms a diagnosis of pulmonary cement embolism.
